name: Eyelash implants

lead: Eyelash implants, also called eyelash transplantation, place hair into the eyelid margin so it grows as lashes. The goal is permanently fuller, more defined eyes without glued-on extensions.

Hair is set into the lid edge so it grows there as lashes. The sources reviewed describe the history of the idea, such as an 1882 report of hair sewn into the eyelids and an 1899 newspaper account, and contain no modern outcome studies.

paras: It is a surgical procedure done on the eyelid, unlike extensions or false lashes that are applied to or alongside existing lashes. People weighing it compare it with those removable options.
It is surgery on the eyelid, and historical accounts describe the early method as painful. No modern safety or outcome studies were found.

angle.text: People seeking permanently fuller lashes consider eyelash transplantation, which places hair into the eyelid margin so it grows as lashes. It differs from extensions and false lashes, and the sources reviewed give history only.

lead: Eyelash implants, also called eyelash transplantation, refer to surgical procedures that place hair into the eyelid margin to create or thicken lashes. They differ from temporary eyelash extensions or false lashes, which are applied to or alongside existing lashes.

Sources reviewed here document the history of related practices rather than modern surgical technique. An 1882 report said Parisians had found a way to make false lashes by having hair sewn into the eyelids, and an 1899 newspaper described a painful method of transplanting scalp hair into the eyelids [1].

paras: Wikipedia's article on eyelash extensions recounts that false eyelashes were patented in the UK by Karl Nessler (filed 1902) and in the US by Anna Taylor (1911), and that in 1916 human-hair lashes fixed with spirit gum were used on actress Seena Owen in the film Intolerance, after which she was reported to have swollen eyes [1]. Temporary lashes became popular in the early 1930s [1].

A registered study examined patient satisfaction with combined botulinum toxin, hyaluronic acid filler and Latisse (a prescription lash-growth product) for facial lines; it does not concern implants [2].
